title: Windsor County holds two of Vermont's 10 most haunted places
excerpt: Two Windsor County places rank among Vermont's 10 most haunted in HauntBound's index, including Springfield's Hartness House Inn at No. 1.
content:
REGION – With Halloween approaching, two Windsor County places rank among Vermont’s 10 most haunted in HauntBound’s 2026 index, including Springfield’s Hartness House Inn at No. 1. The index ranks 34 Vermont sites by separate published accounts and how far back they go, not by fame or search popularity.

The Hartness House Inn ranks No. 1, and no Vermont site has more separate published accounts. James Hartness, a Vermont governor and inventor, built the mansion in 1904, with an underground office and observatory linked by a 240-foot tunnel; aviator Charles Lindbergh stayed in the corner room in 1927. Four separate published accounts describe activity there, the earliest dated to 1927. Guests in that room report a benign child presence known as Charlie, and staff describe a sense of being watched in the basement; the tunnel is linked to electricity cutting out and objects turning up elsewhere.

West Hartford Railroad Bridge ranks No. 8. On Feb. 5, 1887, a Vermont Central night express derailed and caught fire after falling onto the frozen White River, killing roughly 37 people in Vermont’s deadliest train accident; Dartmouth’s Robert Fletcher later traced it to a broken axle. Three separate published accounts describe activity there. Visitors describe the smell of burning wood with no apparent source and cries at night said to echo the wreck.

Statewide, Emily’s Bridge in Stowe, the state’s most famous haunted site, ranks No. 6.

“We rank by evidence, not legend: independent published accounts, documented history, and how far back the reports go. We don’t claim ghosts are real, or that they aren’t. We document where the reports concentrate, and we show our work,” said Ben Fineman, editor of HauntBound. The ranking shows each site’s documented record.

The Hartness House Inn, 109 Front Street in Springfield, is a working inn; guests can also visit the underground tunnel and observatory. West Hartford Railroad Bridge is visible from Route 14 in West Hartford; view from public areas only, and stay off the active rail line.

The full rankings can be found at www.hauntbound.com/most-haunted/vermont.
